submission.justification: Radiator-R3 at 3 cm thickness provides the best pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c with 4.661 sigma, which is approximately 24% better than R1 (3.769 sigma at 4 cm) and 58% better than R2 (2.952 sigma at 3 cm). This meets the primary goal of achieving the best possible separation. The 3 cm thickness is at the optimal point for R3, where performance peaks before declining at greater thicknesses. The dry nitrogen flushing system described in the gas volume documentation should provide adequate environmental control for maintaining radiator performance over the experiment's lifetime. All three radiators are qualified candidates available in the required tile size, and no specific stability or longevity concerns are documented for R3.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c
requirements.evidence: Radiator-R3 at 3 cm provides 4.661 sigma separation, which is the highest among all radiator options and thicknesses tested

requirements.requirement: The radiator must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Radiator-R3 is explicitly listed as one of the three candidate radiators: 'Radiator-R3: high-index porous radiator'

requirements.requirement: The radiator must keep its performance over the experiment's lifetime
requirements.evidence: The vessel is flushed with dry nitrogen during operation, providing environmental control. R3 is listed as a qualified candidate with no documented stability concerns. All candidates are produced in tiles of the required size, suggesting they meet operational requirements.
The recommended thickness of 3 cm is within the specified range of 1-6 cm
